rationale: A 65-year-old male with renal cell carcinoma on ipilimumab and nivolumab developed persistent fevers and generalized FDG-avid lymphadenopathy. Lymph node biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation without visible fungal elements on GMS stain. Comprehensive laboratory workup for histoplasmosis including blood antigen and antibodies was repeatedly negative. Despite negative confirmatory testing, the clinical syndrome was empirically treated with posaconazole and itraconazole with resolution of lymphadenopathy, and the episode was ultimately attributed by the treating clinicians to disseminated histoplasmosis. Because the clinical diagnosis lacks E1 confirmatory pathology/culture/PCR and E2 antigen/antibody evidence, the claim relies entirely on supportive (E3) findings (granulomatous lymphadenopathy, azole response). Under protocol rules, E3 evidence alone cannot establish a verified positive diagnosis -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

Per protocol, remote past infection or presumed etiology without active disease does not satisfy VPD -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Computed tomography of the chest showed findings consistent with miliary TB or histoplasmosis.
empirical therapy against histoplasmosis were initiated.

rationale: A 29-year-old male with HIV and confirmed tuberculosis (MTB-RIF positive) presented with cervical adenomegaly and neurological symptoms. Chest CT demonstrated pulmonary findings consistent with miliary TB or histoplasmosis (E3 supportive imaging), prompting empirical antifungal therapy for histoplasmosis alongside anti-TB treatment. However, no mycological culture, histopathology, PCR, or antigen/antibody assays (E1/E2) were performed or documented to confirm Histoplasma infection. Because the claim relies solely on supportive (E3) radiological suspicion without confirmatory proof, VPD is not satisfied -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: On January 25, 2024, pancytopenia and markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were documented, leading to his admission to the hospital with a diagnosis of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and probable disseminated histoplasmosis-type granulomatous disease.
evidence_items.test_name: Hospital admission clinical evaluation and provisional working diagnosis

step10_contradiction_notes: Provisional admission diagnosis of probable disseminated histoplasmosis without confirmatory microbiological or serological evidence in this CCU text.
rationale: A male patient with newly diagnosed AIDS (CD4 44/mm3) presenting with fever, asthenia, diarrhea, pancytopenia, and markedly elevated LDH (1,860 U/L), leading to admission with a diagnosis of AIDS and probable disseminated histoplasmosis-type granulomatous disease. While the patient exhibited supportive (E3) systemic manifestations of disseminated histoplasmosis, no confirmatory fungal culture, intracellular yeast visualization on histopathology, PCR, or high-titer antigen/antibody results (E1/E2) are documented in this narrative segment. A suspected/probable diagnosis based on E3 supportive clinical evidence alone cannot establish a confirmed case -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: An adult female tiger was presented to the University of Tennessee College of Veterinary Medicine teaching hospital with an acute onset of neurological signs.
Blastomyces and Histoplasma infections are prevalent in Tennessee and are most commonly diagnosed in our laboratory by antigen detection tests offered through a commercial laboratory.

rationale: A veterinary case report describing an adult female tiger presenting with acute neurological signs and pulmonary nodules, diagnosed with disseminated blastomycosis due to Blastomyces gilchristii. Histoplasma is cited only in the background discussion regarding regional fungal prevalence in Tennessee.
